answer: Pay for settling, not for claiming. A head earns only when it repays one real person one real debt - the spool of thread the zephyr took off the line, a season's labour owed - and the lender says on the record that it is cleared. Credit is the scarce input: a lender's book holds one open note at a time, so the same credit cannot stand behind two heads, and a fleet of copies only thins the same lenders' trust. The grove's roll of open notes shows one address stacking them.
